setting: A fictional prospective evaluation in rural localities near Moyobamba, Rioja and Lamas in San Martin, Peru. The places are real; the program, operational records, quantities and planned events are invented.

facts.statement: The partnership wants to learn whether introducing the support package changes nearby forest conversion over two years, alongside household hardship. It has not decided between an effect of an offer to a locality, an effect on participating households or consequences of coverage. It will narrow the question if necessary.
facts.source: Own planning notes from the evaluation meeting
facts.trigger: A question about whose outcomes matter, what decision the study should support, or which effect the researcher wants to estimate.
facts.answer: We want to know whether introducing the package changes nearby forest clearing. We have not decided whether to focus on whole localities or participating households. I am open to narrowing that question.

facts.statement: Every enrolled household is to receive a monthly staple-food basket through a distribution point. Households with school-age children may also receive school-transport seats where service exists. There are no cash payments. Benefits are not conditional on forest conservation, land ownership, research participation or perfect school attendance. Transport availability makes the package heterogeneous.
facts.source: Own notes of the proposed assistance package
facts.trigger: A question about what the program provides, how it differs between households or what conditions attach to benefits.
facts.answer: It is a monthly food basket, with school-transport seats for families with children where that service exists. There is no cash payment or conservation condition. The transport part will differ between places.

facts.statement: The preliminary list contains 84 rural localities in 12 districts and about 3,600 potentially eligible households. Plans call for 30 localities to start in May 2027, 24 in January 2028 and 30 in January 2029. The final wave depends on a future appropriation. These are planned dates, not completed assignments.
facts.source: Own notes of the preliminary rollout calendar
facts.trigger: A question about how many places are involved, when assistance begins or whether everyone starts together.
facts.answer: The first deliveries are provisionally planned for May 2027; none has started.

facts.statement: Managers rank entry using reported food insecurity, transport readiness, storage availability and local administrative capacity. Local representatives can request acceleration after a hardship assessment. There is no lottery or single numerical eligibility cutoff. Dated list versions and minutes will be preserved, but some original telephone discussions were not recorded.
facts.source: Own notes from the rollout-planning discussions
facts.trigger: A question about why areas start at different times, whether assignment is random, or whether a rule or threshold determines eligibility.
facts.answer: Earlier entry depends on hardship, transport readiness, storage and local staffing. Representatives can request priority after a hardship assessment. There is no lottery or single numerical cutoff, and some early telephone discussions were not recorded.

facts.topic: Delivery routes and linked start dates
facts.statement: Localities are settlement clusters rather than independent legal jurisdictions or bounded forest areas. Managers group them into delivery routes. Procurement of a truck and transport contractor often starts several localities on the same route together. The number and membership of final routes have not been fixed.
facts.source: Own notes accompanying the preliminary route map
facts.trigger: A question about whether locality starts are independent, which operational unit determines timing, or how localities share delivery arrangements.
facts.answer: Several localities share each delivery route and usually start together once its truck and contractor are ready. The final route membership and number of routes are not fixed yet.

facts.statement: Researchers cannot change hardship priorities or delay food delivery for a comparison group. They may seek permission to document decisions before implementation, recruit from earlier and later localities and standardize delivery records. Twelve neighboring localities outside the plan have different road access and would require separate participation agreements; their comparability is not established.
facts.source: Own notes of the office's evaluation constraints
facts.trigger: A question about randomizing or changing rollout, delaying assistance, available comparison areas, or what the research team may alter.
facts.answer: We cannot change hardship priorities or delay food deliveries. We can propose data collection in earlier and later localities. Twelve neighboring places might participate, but they have different road access and would need separate agreements.

facts.statement: About 3,600 households appear potentially eligible, but the register has not been verified door to door. Recent arrivals and families away from settlement centers may be missing. Staff verify circumstances and allow appeals. The existing extract has registration date, locality, household size, broad vulnerability indicators and transport requests, but lacks verified farm boundaries and reliable income histories. Managers have not decided whether later waves will use a refreshed household eligibility assessment. Dated copies of each rule version and the date used for each household decision could be requested; retaining shortlist versions alone does not supply that history.
facts.source: Own review notes on the preliminary household register
facts.trigger: A question about recruitment, eligibility lists, who could be omitted, or what household records already contain. Also asks whether household eligibility rules remain comparable across waves or whether their versions and decision dates can be retained.
facts.answer: The register has roughly 3,600 potentially eligible households, but it has not been checked door to door. Recent arrivals and families farther from settlement centers may be missing. Staff will verify eligibility and hear appeals.

facts.topic: Offers, enrollment and receipt can differ
facts.statement: Collection can differ from enrollment because of travel, work, absence, stockouts and sharing food with relatives. Proposed logs can distinguish offers, enrollment, scheduled delivery, collection, basket contents and transport availability, including announcement and notification dates. Staff can add a few fields, but have rejected a second system requiring weekly entry. Route changes, shortages and appeals would use existing records.
facts.source: Own notes on feasible delivery-record changes
facts.trigger: A question about measuring exposure, attendance or actual receipt, documenting rollout changes, or what administrative information can be added.
facts.answer: We can ask for a few fields separating offers, enrollment and actual collection, with dates, basket contents and transport availability. Staff will not maintain a second weekly reporting system. Enrollment does not guarantee that a household collects its basket.

facts.statement: The proposed delivery logs can count collecting households, but no coverage denominator or reference date has been agreed. Possible definitions include collectors among eligible households, collectors among all households, or assistance relative to a mapped area. The household register is incomplete, and the geographic outcome area is unresolved. No verified coverage series exists.
facts.source: Own notes on the proposed coverage measure
facts.trigger: Asks what coverage means, how its denominator or reference date would be defined, or whether planned logs can support a locality coverage measure.
facts.answer: The proposed logs count collecting households, but we have not agreed on a coverage denominator or reference date. The household register is incomplete.

facts.statement: The GIS analyst has public annual forest-loss layers for 2017 through 2024, settlement coordinates, broad land-cover maps and roads. A newer annual layer has not been checked for completeness or consistency. Satellite alerts can guide visits but are not interchangeable with a validated annual forest-loss outcome. None of these archives contains outcomes of the future program.
facts.source: Own notes from the GIS file inventory
facts.trigger: A question about pre-program outcomes, satellite histories, frequency or availability of forest measurements.
facts.answer: We have annual forest-loss layers for 2017 through 2024. A newer layer still needs checking. There are also satellite alerts, but the analyst has not established that they measure the same thing as annual forest loss.

facts.topic: Forest loss is not necessarily conversion
facts.statement: The team has not established how often mapped tree-cover loss represents natural forest converted to another use rather than tree-crop rotation, fire or storm damage. Cloud, small clearings and gradual degradation can obscure changes. Limited participatory mapping and a sample of consented plot visits are possible proposals, but their extent and budget allocation are not fixed. A complete cadastral survey is unaffordable. No pre-program natural-forest mask, classification rule or baseline reference date has been chosen. The broad land-cover files have not been checked for distinguishing plantations from natural forest. The land contributing to the outcome remains a planning choice.
facts.source: Own notes of unresolved forest-measurement questions
facts.trigger: A question about what forest loss means, measurement error, validating satellite outcomes or affordable ground checks. Also asks which land counts as forest at baseline, the reference date, or how plantations would be distinguished.
facts.answer: We do not yet know how often the mapped losses are permanent forest conversion rather than crop rotation, fire or storm damage. Limited mapping and consented plot visits might help, but we cannot afford a complete land survey.

facts.statement: Settlement-centered circles need not match resource-use areas. Some households farm dispersed or rented plots, and some use collectively managed land. Neighboring settlements may share forest. Existing boundary files overlap or leave gaps; verified household farm boundaries do not exist. A stable geographic outcome area still needs definition before later changes are examined.
facts.source: Own notes of the mapping discussion
facts.trigger: A question about linking forest change to households or localities, plot boundaries, buffers or the geographical outcome unit.
facts.answer: We do not have verified household farm boundaries. Families may use scattered, rented or shared land, and locality boundaries overlap or have gaps. A circle around a settlement would not necessarily describe the forest its households use.

facts.statement: The draft budget is S/480,000 over 26 months for coordination, part-time GIS work, enumerators, travel and data management. It supports about 720 households across 60 localities at baseline and two returns. Covering all 84 would require fewer interviews per locality or shorter questionnaires. Limited mapping must compete within this budget; no additional funds are confirmed and the exact tradeoff is not costed. Phone coverage is uneven.
facts.source: Own notes of the draft fieldwork budget
facts.trigger: A question about sample size, funds, fieldwork capacity, adding measurements or tradeoffs between households and localities.
facts.answer: The draft funding supports a baseline survey and two return visits to the same households.

facts.topic: Household information that could still be collected
facts.statement: A pre-delivery survey could record residence history, composition, food insecurity, earnings sources, crop calendars, shocks, land use, informal support, school travel and market access. There is no existing household panel on these topics. Questionnaire length remains negotiable. Survey responses would be prospective measurements, not proof that every relevant determinant of rollout or forest use has been measured.
facts.source: Own notes of the draft baseline questionnaire
facts.trigger: A question about available household history, possible baseline variables or what interviews could measure before the program.
facts.answer: We could ask about residence, household composition, food insecurity, earnings, crops, recent shocks, land use, informal help, school travel and market access before deliveries. There is no existing household panel, and the questionnaire can still be shortened.

facts.statement: The team wants to revisit original respondents even if they stop collecting benefits, become ineligible or move. Tracking outside the study provinces has not been costed. Refusals should be recorded without program staff present. Telephone access is uneven, and there is no evidence establishing the future amount or causes of loss to follow-up.
facts.source: Own notes of the proposed follow-up arrangements
facts.trigger: A question about attrition, migration, following nonrecipients or whether household outcomes will remain available.
facts.answer: We want to revisit original respondents even if they stop collecting assistance or move. Tracking beyond the study provinces has not been costed, and telephone access is uneven. We do not know how many people we might lose.

facts.statement: Fieldwork must be booked in March 2027. The office needs an implementation brief in September 2028. Household interviews are funded only through April 2029; forest monitoring could continue through December 2029. January 2029 entrants therefore cannot contribute two full post-start years. A common horizon or narrower cohort set has not been agreed.
facts.source: Own notes of the funding and decision calendar
facts.trigger: A question about study duration, follow-up, reporting deadlines or when a decision must be made.
facts.answer: An implementation brief is due in September 2028. Interviews are funded through April 2029, and forest monitoring could continue through December 2029. Places starting in January 2029 would therefore have less follow-up than the others.

facts.topic: Roads and other changing local conditions
facts.statement: Road readiness affects delivery and can also change markets and land demand. Hardship, commodity prices, weather, fires, tenure changes and conservation activities may differ between localities. Access to district road-maintenance plans and land-use or conservation maps has been requested but not granted. Some records use outdated locality names. Overlap with other household-assistance schemes has not been checked.
facts.source: Own notes on contextual records and outstanding access requests
facts.trigger: A question about other explanations for forest change, road projects, concurrent programs or available contextual records.
facts.answer: We have requested road-maintenance and land-use records but do not yet have permission to use them. We also have not checked which households receive other assistance. Road improvements could affect both delivery readiness and farming opportunities.

facts.statement: Relatives can share food across locality boundaries, neighboring settlements may share forest and transport contractors may serve nearby places. Clearing could move outside the selected geographic outcome area. These are plausible pathways, not observed program effects. The team has not measured their size or settled a coverage-based target.
facts.source: Own notes of practical concerns raised before implementation
facts.trigger: A question about contamination, shared forests, indirect effects, coverage or activity moving outside the study area.
facts.answer: Families sometimes share food with relatives in other localities, and settlements may use the same forest. We do not know how much the program might affect neighboring places or shift clearing beyond whichever area we map.

facts.statement: Research participation must not affect support eligibility. Discussions need appropriate local languages. Community permission does not replace individual consent; an individual's interview consent does not settle permission for mapping collectively used land. No research approval or permission to enter private or collectively managed land has been obtained simply by preparing the study notes.
facts.source: Own notes of community concerns and current permission status
facts.trigger: A question about consent, community involvement, research approval, access to land or making participation a condition of assistance.
facts.answer: Families must be able to refuse research without losing support. Community leaders cannot consent for each household, and interviews would not automatically permit mapping shared land. Research and land-access permissions are not yet in place.

facts.statement: The identifier crosswalk stays with the administrative custodian. The proposed agreement separates identifiers from analysis and restricts precise plot disclosure, but it is unsigned. Confidentiality promises under land disputes or official requests need clarification. Public maps alleging illegal activity or lists of nonparticipants are outside the proposal. Household hardship and land-use questions can cause stigma or disputes.
facts.source: Own notes of the draft research and data-access agreement
facts.trigger: A question about privacy, data linkage, disclosing plots or whether sensitive land-use information can be safely collected.
facts.answer: The custodian would keep the identifier crosswalk, and precise plot locations would be restricted. The agreement is still unsigned. We need to clarify what confidentiality we can promise, especially if land disputes or official requests arise.

facts.topic: Why the forest effect could go either way
facts.statement: Assistance could reduce pressure to clear after income shocks, but it could also finance farming activity, change labor allocation or shift demand to products from elsewhere. These are hypotheses only. The coordinator does not know the direction of the future effect and does not equate a locality-level forest change with a household-specific mechanism.
facts.source: Own notes of the motivation for the future study
facts.trigger: A question about the expected direction, the mechanism of forest change or which household behaviors might change.
facts.answer: We hope the support reduces pressure to clear land after bad harvests, but it might also free resources for farming. We do not know which would dominate, and no program outcomes have happened yet.

world_only.statement: This is a fictional adaptation for evaluating consultation behavior, not evidence about an actual Peruvian assistance program. Real locations do not make the invented dates, budget, rollout or institutions factual. Original-paper identity and findings belong only in the separate story provenance materials.
At the frozen planning date, the intervention has not begun and no program-effect outcome exists. The packet supplies no numerical causal truth, favored estimator or required effect direction.

adaptation_notes: Retains the fictional story's planning date, location, in-kind package, rollout calendar, nonrandom priorities, route grouping, budget, measurement gaps and permissions.
Converts the narrative into semantically triggered fact cards, with core topic markers for author review. Core markers are not an actor disclosure quota or a fixed conversation sequence.
The full story and provenance are reviewer-side context. The actor uses selected practical knowledge only, and the consultant begins with the short future-study request.
The budget card clarifies that proposed mapping competes with other activities inside the existing draft budget; it does not invent a separately costed mapping option or confirmed additional funding.
This is a focused planning consultation. A useful collection and conditional analysis plan can complete it without producing a numerical effect estimate or saved HTML report.

Case/world 1.1.0 adopts only the three prioritized refinements in validation/paper-enrichment-forest.md: eligibility-rule history, a coverage denominator and reference date, and a pre-program forest definition. The original source story is preserved as a foundation. These added fictional unknowns and collection options do not establish new access, stable eligibility or a required analysis route.

data_status: No future outcomes or causal effect are generated. Statements describe fictional planning facts or explicitly unresolved questions.
